rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish whether combining RNA and image data improves performance. This experiment tests the impact of multimodal fusion (concat) with simple encoders (pca_n2000 for RNA, resnet50 for image) and no aggregation, which directly addresses whether multimodal approaches are worth exploring. It is the best use of the first experiment as it reduces uncertainty about the most critical design choice: whether multimodal modeling provides value.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 have moderate performance. This experiment tests the impact of changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' in the same configuration, clarifying whether fusion strategy significantly affects performance. It is the best next step as it directly addresses a key design choice (fusion method) with minimal parameter changes, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with singleprofile, pca_n2000, and resnet50 achieve ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests multimodal multiprofile with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, addressing uncertainty about profile settings and aggregation methods. It balances exploration of key design choices (profile setting, aggregation) while building on prior multimodal experiments.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups with avgpool aggregation (config_018, 0.618 accuracy) outperform singleprofile and other aggregation methods. This experiment tests whether changing fusion from concat to weighted (config_019) further improves performance, clarifying if fusion method matters in this high-performing context. It directly extends the most successful configuration, balancing exploitation of proven effectiveness with exploration of key design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve high validation accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 in this promising configuration improves performance, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the multiprofile/weighted fusion direction with exploration of encoder variations.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieves high validation accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation while retaining weighted fusion could further improve performance. This clarifies the impact of aggregation method on model performance, a key design choice, while building on the promising scvi_n200 and weighted fusion combination.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l (config_039) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using scgpt RNA encoder with the same aggregation and weighted fusion could further improve performance, clarifying the impact of RNA encoder choice and fusion method.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder, aggregation, and concat fusion, which could clarify whether scgpt is a better RNA encoder or if the fusion type (concat vs weighted) is critical. It is informative despite lower expected performance, as it addresses uncertainty about RNA encoder choice and fusion method impact.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_033: 0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) in config_033 improves performance. It clarifies the impact of image encoder choice on performance while maintaining the proven-effective aggregation and fusion strategies.

Existing evidence shows that using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l (config_039) achieves high performance. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt and image encoder with resnet50 (while retaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion) could further improve performance. It clarifies the importance of RNA/image encoder choices versus aggregation/fusion methods, which are critical design decisions. This is the best use of the next experiment as it explores a key uncertainty while building on a promising direction.
